sentence: A high CRP means there is inflammation or infection somewhere in the body, but not where or why, so doctors read it with symptoms and other tests.
note: LTO: high or rising CRP suggests acute infection or inflammation but does not identify location or cause

sentence: CRP stands for C-reactive protein, a protein that the liver makes.
note: MedlinePlus: CRP is a protein made by the liver

sentence: Its level in the blood rises when there is inflammation somewhere in the body.
note: LTO: CRP rises with inflammation

sentence: Tissue injury, infection and other kinds of inflammation can all push the level up.
note: MedlinePlus: rises after tissue injury, infection or other inflammation

sentence: Doctors usually request the test when they suspect an infection or inflammation, for example after surgery.
note: LTO: requested when acute inflammation is a risk (for example infection after surgery) or suspected from symptoms

sentence: It is also used to help assess long-term inflammatory conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis and lupus.
note: LTO: requested to evaluate chronic inflammatory conditions, rheumatoid arthritis and lupus named

sentence: The sample is taken from a vein, and the sources list no special preparation.
note: LTO: no test preparation needed; venous sample is the usual route (textbook)

sentence: A high or rising CRP suggests that there is an acute infection or inflammation.
note: LTO/MedlinePlus: high or increasing CRP suggests acute infection or inflammation

sentence: It does not show where the inflammation is or which condition is causing it.
note: both: does not help identify location or condition

sentence: For that reason the test is not diagnostic on its own.
note: LTO: the test is not diagnostic

sentence: Lab Tests Online UK adds that CRP is not specific for bacterial infection and is raised in many other conditions as well.
note: LTO news piece: CRP not specific for bacterial infection, frequently elevated in a wide range of other conditions

sentence: A small rise is hard to interpret by itself, so doctors consider it alongside the whole clinical picture.
note: StatPearls: marginal increases are difficult to interpret and should not be used as an isolated result

sentence: In someone who already has a long-term inflammatory condition, a high level can point to a flare-up or to treatment that is not working.
note: LTO: in chronic conditions high level can signal flare or that treatment is not working

sentence: The cause of a high CRP cannot always be found.
note: MedlinePlus: cause of high CRP cannot always be determined

sentence: MedlinePlus lists cancer, heart attack, infection, inflammatory bowel disease, rheumatoid arthritis, lupus and related diseases, and rheumatic fever among the conditions that can raise CRP.
note: MedlinePlus list of possible causes

sentence: Not every cause is an illness.
note: LTO lists physiological causes (see next sentence); phrasing is the author's

sentence: CRP can be higher in the later stages of pregnancy, in women who use the contraceptive pill and in women who take hormone replacement therapy.
note: both state this

sentence: Lab Tests Online UK also links obesity with higher levels.
note: LTO: obesity linked to higher levels

sentence: StatPearls describes smoking, diabetes and other long-term conditions as associated with low-grade inflammation that can raise CRP.
note: StatPearls (blended summary): obesity, smoking, metabolic syndrome, diabetes, insomnia associated with low-grade inflammation and elevated CRP; second pass to confirm

sentence: The doctor reads the result alongside signs and symptoms, a physical examination and other tests.
note: LTO: doctors use CRP with symptoms, exam and other tests

sentence: That can help show whether someone has an acute inflammatory condition or a flare-up of a long-term one.
note: LTO: to determine acute inflammatory condition or flare of chronic disease

sentence: The doctor may then arrange further tests or treatment.
note: LTO: doctor may follow up with further testing and treatment

sentence: The test is often repeated to follow progress, because CRP falls as inflammation settles.
note: LTO: repeated to track progress; levels drop as inflammation subsides

sentence: A falling level suggests that the inflammation is easing.
note: LTO

sentence: Lab Tests Online UK says results from a test requested by a GP take about seven working days on average to come back from the hospital.
note: LTO: on average 7 working days, depending on tests requested

sentence: A CRP result does not say how urgent an illness is, so severe symptoms such as sudden chest pain or collapse need a 999 call, and feeling more and more unwell needs NHS 111 or the GP the same day.
note: signposting sentence; 999 for chest pain from NHS heart-attack page; the rest is standard NHS signposting

sentence: High-sensitivity CRP, or hs-CRP, is a separate and more sensitive version of the test.
note: LTO hs-CRP page: hs-CRP separate, more sensitive

sentence: It has been used to estimate the risk of heart disease in people who seem healthy.
note: LTO hs-CRP page

sentence: Lab Tests Online UK notes that current UK guidelines on cardiovascular risk assessment do not recommend hs-CRP testing.
note: LTO hs-CRP page

sentence: StatPearls states that some medicines, including non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and statins, can lower CRP.
note: StatPearls (blended summary): NSAIDs and statins can reduce CRP; second pass to confirm

sentence: Long-term conditions linked with low-grade inflammation can lift it.
note: same blended summary

sentence: Because of these influences, a single value is rarely read on its own.
note: author inference from StatPearls caution on isolated results

sentence: A high CRP shows that inflammation or infection is likely, but it does not show where it is or what is causing it.
note: as above

sentence: CRP is a protein made by the liver that rises after tissue injury, infection or other inflammation.
note: MedlinePlus: CRP is made by the liver; rises after injury, infection, other inflammation

sentence: Doctors read the result together with symptoms, an examination and other tests, and often repeat it to see which way it is going.
note: LTO: used with signs, symptoms, exam and other tests; often repeated to track progress

sentence: A high CRP can have causes that are not diseases, such as later pregnancy, the contraceptive pill or hormone replacement therapy.
note: both list pregnancy, contraceptive pill and HRT

sentence: The laboratory report shows the reference range used, and ranges differ between laboratories.
note: LTO notes ranges vary by laboratory; NHS lab directory pages give their own ranges
